content.user_title: Publish Azure Event Grid Events in Python
content.value_statement: Publishing Azure Event Grid events from Python requires choosing schemas, credentials, endpoints, and client patterns. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for safe SDK setup and event publishing.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install azure-eventgrid and azure-identity.
Explains topic and namespace endpoint variables for Event Grid.
Provides examples for CloudEvent and EventGridEvent publishing.
Covers sync, batch, async, and namespace topic sending.
limitations: It does not create Azure Event Grid topics or namespaces.
It does not manage event subscriptions, dead-lettering, or handlers.
Examples require existing Azure credentials and endpoints.
It does not validate business payload schemas.

use_cases.title: Add event publishing to a Python service
use_cases.description: Build a clear Event Grid publishing flow with authentication, endpoints, and event payload structure.

use_cases.title: Choose an event schema for integration
use_cases.description: Compare CloudEvents and EventGridEvent formats for interoperability and Azure-native workflows.

use_cases.title: Plan higher-throughput publishing
use_cases.description: Use batching and async client guidance when services need to publish many events.

prompt_templates.title: Create basic setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up a Python project to publish Azure Event Grid events. Include required packages, endpoint variables, and authentication choices.

prompt_templates.title: Build CloudEvent publisher
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a Python publishing flow for CloudEvents using EventGridPublisherClient. Explain event type, source, subject, payload, and batching decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Convert to async publishing
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor my Event Grid publisher design for async sending. Include credential handling, batching, retry awareness, and clean client shutdown.

prompt_templates.title: Design namespace workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a pull-delivery Event Grid namespace topic workflow for Python publishers. Compare topic endpoints, namespace endpoints, and operational checks.

output_examples.input: I need to publish order events from a Python service.
output: A setup checklist with SDK packages, endpoint variables, and credential requirements.
A CloudEvents publishing plan with event type, source, subject, payload, and batching guidance.
Notes on retries, filtering subjects, and safe production rollout.
An async client design with credential lifetime guidance.
Batching recommendations for groups of related events.
Operational notes for retry behavior and clean shutdown.

output_examples.input: I am using Event Grid namespace topics.
output: A namespace publishing checklist with endpoint and topic-name guidance.
A comparison of custom topic and namespace endpoint patterns.
Questions to confirm pull-delivery assumptions before implementation.

best_practices: Use CloudEvents for new applications when interoperability matters.
Batch related events when throughput is important.
Choose meaningful subjects and event types for filtering.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode real endpoints or secrets in application source.
Do not publish vague event types that subscribers cannot filter.
Do not use sync publishing for high-throughput workloads without measuring latency.

faq.question: Does this skill create Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Python SDK publishing guidance for existing Event Grid resources.

faq.question: Which event format should I use?
faq.answer: Use CloudEvents for new applications unless you need Azure-native EventGridEvent schema.

faq.question: Can it help with authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows DefaultAzureCredential usage and explains endpoint configuration.

faq.question: Does it cover async publishing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes async client examples for higher-throughput publishers.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it send events automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Your environment controls any actual Azure calls.
